entries.name: block-depth-left-then-plain-accept#0
entries.description: Block section (version 4) with two transactions. Tx A's only output has the size-flagged v3 tree BoolToSigmaProp(LogicalNot^107(0xfd)), which degrades 109 levels deep and leaves those levels on its reader. Tx B has an ordinary sigmaProp(true) output. The JVM parses each transaction on a fresh SigmaByteReader, so tx B starts at level 0 and the section round-trips. On one shared reader, tx B's plain tree would need levels 110 and 111: an impl that shares reader state across transactions rejects the section.

entries.name: block-plain-then-depth-left-accept#1
entries.description: The same two transactions, the ordinary one first: nothing follows the degrade, so even a shared reader accepts. The control for #0.

entries.name: block-valdef-then-valuse-reject#2
entries.description: Block section: tx A's output tree is BlockValue(ValDef(1, SigmaProp(true)), ValUse(1)); tx B's is 00 72 01, the bare ValUse(1). Tx B parses on a fresh reader whose ValDef store is empty, so ValUse(1) throws NoSuchElementException and the JVM rejects the section. On one shared reader tx A's ValDef(1) would resolve it: an impl that shares reader state across transactions round-trips the section, the over-accept.

entries.name: block-valdef-then-own-valdef-accept#3
entries.description: The twin of #2: tx B's tree defines its own ValDef(1). Round-trip identity.
